module_title: Political Turbulence, Poverty Removal, and Rolling Plans (4th to 7th)
introduction: This era is defined by Indira Gandhi’s leadership, slogans of 'Garibi Hatao', and the first taste of political instability impacting economic planning.

core_concepts.title: Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)
core_concepts.description: Objective: 'Growth with Stability and Self-reliance'. Major events: Nationalization of 14 major banks (1969) and the first nuclear test at Pokhran (Operation Smiling Buddha, 1974).

core_concepts.title: Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978)
core_concepts.description: Focus: 'Garibi Hatao' (Poverty Removal) and Self-reliance. It launched the 'Minimum Needs Programme'. Crucially, this plan only lasted 4 years because the new Janta Party government terminated it in 1978.

core_concepts.title: Rolling Plan (1978-1980)
core_concepts.description: The Janta Party government introduced this concept based on Gunnar Myrdal’s book 'Asian Drama'. It replaced the fixed 5-year cycle with a flexible 'Rolling' model.

core_concepts.title: Sixth (1980-85) and Seventh (1985-90) Plans
core_concepts.description: 6th Plan: Marked the return of Indira Gandhi and focused on poverty alleviation and the establishment of NABARD (1982). 7th Plan: Focused on food-grain production and 'Employment Generation'. It broke the 'Hindu Rate of Growth' barrier.

important_entities.name: Garibi Hatao Slogan
important_entities.significance: While the slogan was given during the 1971 elections, it became the official objective of the 5th Five-Year Plan.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Question: 'Which Five-Year Plan was terminated one year before its schedule?' Answer: The 5th Five-Year Plan (1974-1978).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 78-80: The Roller came over the Plan
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1978-80 was the duration of the Rolling Plan after the Janta Party came to power.

exam_strategy_tips: Bank Nationalization (1969) = 4th Plan. NABARD setup (1982) = 6th Plan. These are recurring years in GS papers.
